---
title: "Solow growth model with growing technology: an investment rate shock"
page-layout: full
toc: false
---

{{< include _sequence.qmd >}}

This is the [Solow growth model with growing technology](effective.qmd), with a
permanent change in the investment rate, $s$, partway through the
simulation.^[Textbooks usually call $s$ the *saving rate*; see the note on the [first page](index.qmd).]

Press play, or drag the time slider, to follow the economy from its initial
capital stock $k_0$. When the shock arrives, the investment curve shifts and the
economy heads for a new steady state; the old curve stays on the diagram as a
dashed line for comparison. In the charts over time, a dotted vertical line marks
the shock, and the steady-state level of $k$ steps to its new value. Growth of GDP
per capita jumps and then falls back to the rate of technology, $g$: a higher
investment rate raises the level of GDP per capita, not its long-run growth rate.

::: {.sim-layout .column-screen-inset}

::: {.sim-controls}


```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof sShock = Inputs.range([0.01, 0.6], {value: 0.35, step: 0.01, label: "Investment rate after shock"})
viewof shockT = Inputs.range([1, periods - 1], {value: periods / 2, step: 1, label: "Shock period"})
```
